info.name: FieldOps System Backend
info.description:
API collection for the FieldOps backend — Express 5 + Prisma 7 + PostgreSQL, with Redis-backed OTP auth, Cloudinary uploads and Stripe payments.

**Getting started**
1. Set `baseUrl` (default `http://localhost:5000`, matching `PORT` in `.env`).
2. Run the collection-level pre-request script once — it generates `{{futureDate}}`, `{{futureDateIso}}` and `{{stripeSignature}}` for you.
3. Hit Login. The test scripts decode the JWT and fill in `{{accessToken}}` plus the role-scoped `{{adminAccessToken}}` / `{{technicianAccessToken}}` / `{{customerAccessToken}}`, so switch roles by logging in as that role.
4. IDs are chained automatically: Get All Services sets `{{serviceId}}`, Get All Technicians sets `{{technicianId}}`, Create Availability sets `{{availabilityId}}`, Create Booking sets `{{bookingId}}`, and so on. The booking, payment and review flows each need their matching role token.

**Conventions**
- Every response uses the envelope `{ success, statusCode, message, data, meta? }`; paginated endpoints add `meta: { page, limit, total, totalPages }`.
- `Content-Type: application/json` on JSON bodies. Endpoints with file uploads use multipart/form-data, so they deliberately carry no `Content-Type` header — Postman sets the boundary itself.
- Query filters that look boolean (`isActive`, `isBooked`, `isAvailable`) are validated as the **strings** `"true"` / `"false"`, while `isActive` in an Update Service body is a real boolean.

**Known behaviour**
`globalErrorHandler` computes a `statusCode` but always responds with HTTP 500, so auth failures, role violations, Zod validation failures and `AppError`s such as 404 / 409 all arrive as 500 with the real reason in `message` (in `NODE_ENV=development`). The one exception is unmatched routes, which return a genuine 404. Assertions here check for success rather than specific error codes.

item.name: Health
item.description: Liveness probe for the Express app. No auth required.

request.description: Basic route registered in `src/app.ts`. Confirms the server is up and reachable.

Any unmatched path falls through to `notFound` middleware and returns 404. Useful for checking that a route you expect really does not exist.

Note: unlike other failures, the 404 handler responds with the real HTTP 404 status.

item.name: Auth
item.description:
Public auth endpoints under `/api/v1/auth`. Registration and password reset send 6-digit OTPs by email (stored in Redis for 5 minutes) — paste the OTP into `{{otp}}` before running the verification step.

The login-style requests decode the returned JWT and store `userId`, `userRole` and the role-scoped `adminAccessToken` / `technicianAccessToken` / `customerAccessToken`.

request.description:
Creates a pending registration and emails a 6-digit OTP. Password rules: min 8 chars, at least one uppercase, one lowercase, one number and one special character. `phone` is optional.

Re-running with the same email fails until the account exists — use a fresh email or reset with Forgot Password.
Verifies the emailed OTP, creates the user, sends the welcome email and returns the user plus both tokens. Captures `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `userId` and the role-scoped tokens.

Credential login. Same password rules as registration are enforced on the payload.

Server seeds an ADMIN, a TECHNICIAN and a CUSTOMER on boot — their emails and passwords come from `ADMIN_EMAIL` / `TECHNICIAN_EMAIL` / `CUSTOMER_EMAIL` in `.env`. Log in as each role when you need to hit role-guarded endpoints.

Exchanges a Google ID token for API tokens, creating the user on first sign-in. `idToken` must be issued for the `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` in `.env`, and the token must carry both `email` and `name` claims.

No Zod validation on this route — an unverifiable token throws "Invalid Or Expired Google Id Token".

Rotates the pair: returns a fresh access token and refresh token. The refresh token is read from the `refreshToken` cookie if present, otherwise from the body — this request sends it in the body.

The user must still exist and be `ACTIVE`.

Note: the server does not currently set cookies itself, so the body field is what actually gets used here.
Emails a password-reset OTP (5 minute TTL in Redis). Only available for `CREDENTIAL` accounts — Google-only accounts get "User has account with google". Banned users are rejected.

Consumes the OTP from Forgot Password and sets the new password (hashed with bcrypt). `newPassword` follows the same complexity rules as registration.

Update `{{password}}` after this so later Login requests keep working.

Requires `CUSTOMER`, `TECHNICIAN` or `ADMIN` — any authenticated caller. `password` is omitted. Captures `userId` from the response.

The auth middleware matches the JWT against the database on `id` + `email` + `name` + `role`, so changing your name or email invalidates tokens issued before the change.

request.description:
Requires `CUSTOMER`, `TECHNICIAN` or `ADMIN`.

multipart/form-data. `name` (2-100 chars) and `phone` (6-20 chars) are optional; `avatar` is an optional image uploaded to Cloudinary. Uploading a new avatar deletes the previous Cloudinary asset.

Changing `name` invalidates your current access token because the middleware matches the JWT name against the stored user.

item.name: Services
item.description: Catalog endpoints under `/api/v1/services`. Reads are public; writes require `ADMIN`. Service deletion is a soft delete (`isActive = false`) and also removes the image from Cloudinary.

query.description: "true" or "false" only — anything else fails validation.

request.description:
Public, paginated list. Query is validated with Zod: `page` and `limit` are coerced to numbers, and `limit` is capped at 100. Pagination metadata comes back under `meta`.

Captures the first result id into `{{serviceId}}` so the requests below have something to work with.

request.description: Public lookup of a single service by id.

formdata.value: Professional AC repair and maintenance for residential and commercial properties.

request.description:
Requires `ADMIN`. multipart/form-data because of the optional `image` upload.

Validation: `title` 3-100 chars, `slug` lowercase-with-hyphens (`/^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$/`), `description` min 10 chars, `category` min 2 chars, `price` > 0, `duration` positive integer. `slug` is unique — reusing one returns 409 "A service with this slug already exists".

Captures `{{serviceId}}`.

response.name: Duplicate slug (reported as HTTP 500)

formdata.description: Optional. Must stay unique across services.
Optional. true / false — sent as a text field in form-data.

request.description: Requires `ADMIN`. multipart/form-data. Every field is optional; `isActive` is a real JSON boolean here (unlike the query filters, which expect the strings "true"/"false"). Supplying a new `image` deletes the previous Cloudinary asset.
Requires `ADMIN`. Soft delete: sets `isActive = false` rather than removing the row, and deletes the Cloudinary image if one is attached. Existing bookings keep their reference to the service.

item.name: Technicians
item.description:
Technician profiles under `/api/v1/technicians`. Browsing is public; anything that touches a profile requires the `TECHNICIAN` role.

A technician profile only exists after the user calls Create Technician Profile — until then the profile-scoped routes return "Technician profile not found".

request.description:
Public, paginated list of technician profiles with their user details, aggregate rating and availability flag.

Captures the first profile id into `{{technicianId}}` — note this is the `TechnicianProfile.id`, which is what bookings and availability routes expect, not the underlying user id.
Public profile lookup. Captures `{{technicianId}}` so this can be used to seed the variable before creating a booking.

formdata.value: Certified HVAC technician with 8 years of experience in residential and commercial systems.

formdata.description: Optional. Stored in Cloudinary and mirrored to the user avatar.

request.description:
Requires `TECHNICIAN`. multipart/form-data for the optional `profileImage`, which is also written back to the user avatar.

Validation: `experience` integer 0-50, `specialization` 2-100 chars, `hourlyRate` > 0, `bio` optional 10-500 chars. One profile per user — a second call returns 409 "Technician profile already exists".

Captures `{{technicianId}}`.
Requires `TECHNICIAN`. Returns the caller's own profile with the related user record.

formdata.value: Senior HVAC technician specialising in commercial cooling systems.

request.description: Requires `TECHNICIAN`. multipart/form-data. All fields optional — this is the partial form of the create schema, so `experience` and `hourlyRate` can be changed without resending everything. A new `profileImage` replaces the old Cloudinary asset.
Requires `TECHNICIAN`. Flips the profile-level `isAvailable` flag that customers see when browsing. This is separate from individual availability slots under `/availability`.

item.name: Availability
item.description:
Time slots under `/api/v1/availability`. Creating, editing and deleting requires `TECHNICIAN`; reading a technician's public slots is open.

Slots cannot be in the past, must satisfy `startTime < endTime`, and cannot overlap another slot for the same technician on the same day. Booked slots are locked — updates and deletes are rejected until the booking is cancelled.

request.description:
Requires `TECHNICIAN`. `date` must be a full ISO datetime (Zod `datetime()`), not a bare date — `{{futureDateIso}}` is generated for you by the collection-level pre-request script. Times are `HH:MM` 24-hour strings.

Captures `{{availabilityId}}`, which Create Booking needs.

response.name: Overlapping slot (reported as HTTP 500)

request.description:
Requires `TECHNICIAN`. Paginated list of the caller's slots. Note the default page size here is 20, not 10.

Captures the first slot id into `{{availabilityId}}`.

Public list of a technician's slots, used by customers to pick a time. When `isBooked` is omitted the service defaults to free slots only.

Captures the first slot id into `{{availabilityId}}`.
Requires `TECHNICIAN`, and only for a slot the caller owns. All fields optional, but the same past-date, time-order and overlap checks apply. Booked slots cannot be edited.
Requires `TECHNICIAN`, and only for a slot the caller owns. Booked slots cannot be deleted — cancel the booking first, which frees the slot.

item.name: Bookings
item.description:
Booking lifecycle under `/api/v1/bookings`. Customers create, list, cancel and read bookings; technicians list their own queue and drive status transitions.

Valid transitions: PENDING to ACCEPTED / REJECTED / CANCELLED, ACCEPTED to IN_PROGRESS / CANCELLED, IN_PROGRESS to COMPLETED / CANCELLED. COMPLETED, REJECTED and CANCELLED are terminal. REJECTING or CANCELLING frees the availability slot.

body.raw:
{
  "technicianId": "{{technicianId}}",
  "serviceId": "{{serviceId}}",
  "availabilityId": "{{availabilityId}}",
  "address": "House 12, Road 5, Dhanmondi, Dhaka",
  "problemDescription": "AC is not cooling properly and needs a gas refill and compressor check."
}

request.description:
Requires `CUSTOMER`. All ids must be valid UUIDs: `technicianId` (a TechnicianProfile id), `serviceId`, and `availabilityId` (an unbooked, unrequested slot belonging to that technician). `address` is 10-500 chars, `problemDescription` 10-1000 chars.

Creates the booking as PENDING, prices it from the service and marks the slot as booked, all in one transaction. Captures `{{bookingId}}`.

query.description: PENDING | ACCEPTED | REJECTED | IN_PROGRESS | COMPLETED | CANCELLED

request.description:
Requires `CUSTOMER`. Paginated bookings for the caller with service, technician, availability, payment and review expanded.

Captures the first booking id into `{{bookingId}}`.

query.description: PENDING | ACCEPTED | REJECTED | IN_PROGRESS | COMPLETED | CANCELLED

request.description:
Requires `TECHNICIAN`. The technician-side view of the same booking list, with the customer record expanded.

Captures the first booking id into `{{bookingId}}`.
Requires `CUSTOMER` or `TECHNICIAN`, and only if the caller is the booking's customer or its assigned technician. Returns the full relation graph.

Requires `TECHNICIAN`, and only for a booking assigned to them. Body is a single `status` field; `PENDING` is not accepted here because the transition out of it is ACCEPTED, REJECTED or CANCELLED.

Run these in order to walk a booking to completion: ACCEPTED -> IN_PROGRESS -> COMPLETED. Rejecting or cancelling frees the availability slot.

response.name: Illegal transition

request.description: Requires `CUSTOMER`, and only for the caller's own booking while it is still PENDING or ACCEPTED. Sets status CANCELLED and releases the availability slot in the same transaction.

item.name: Payments
item.description: Stripe-backed payments under `/api/v1/payments`. A booking must be ACCEPTED before checkout, and each booking can have at most one payment record.

request.description:
Requires `CUSTOMER`. Body is just `bookingId` (UUID). The booking must be ACCEPTED and unpaid. Creates or updates the payment record as PENDING with the Checkout Session id as `transactionId`, and returns the hosted `checkoutUrl` plus `sessionId` and the amount in the major currency unit (Stripe receives cents).

Captures `{{sessionId}}` and `{{checkoutUrl}}`.

header.description: Signature from the Stripe-Secret header. Generated for you by the collection pre-request script.

request.description:
Called by Stripe, not by clients. Handled on a dedicated `express.raw` mount in `src/app.ts`, which runs before the JSON body parser so the raw payload stays byte-exact for signature verification. A missing `stripe-signature` header returns 400.

Handles `checkout.session.completed` (payment -> PAID, stamps `paidAt`) and `payment_intent.payment_failed` (payment -> FAILED). The upsert is keyed on the unique `bookingId`, so replays are idempotent.

The signature must match `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Hand-rolled payloads fail verification, so use `stripe listen --forward-to localhost:5000/api/v1/payments/webhook` for a real test.
Requires `CUSTOMER`. Paginated payment history with the related booking expanded. Captures the first payment id into `{{paymentId}}`.
Requires `CUSTOMER`, and only for a payment on one of the caller's own bookings. Returns the payment with the full booking relation graph.

item.name: Reviews
item.description: Reviews under `/api/v1/reviews`. A review requires the booking to be COMPLETED and paid, and there can be only one per booking. Every write recalculates the technician's aggregate `rating` and `totalReviews`.

request.description:
Requires `CUSTOMER`. `bookingId` must be a UUID for one of your own COMPLETED bookings whose payment is PAID, and it must not already be reviewed. `rating` is an integer 1-5; `comment` is optional up to 1000 chars.

Captures `{{reviewId}}`.
Public, paginated reviews for a technician with the reviewer expanded. Captures the first review id into `{{reviewId}}`.
Public lookup of a single review. Captures `{{reviewId}}`.
Requires `CUSTOMER`, and only on your own review. Both fields optional. The technician aggregate rating is recomputed from the remaining reviews.
Requires `CUSTOMER`, and only on your own review. Deleting recalculates the technician's aggregate rating and review count.

item.name: Analytics
item.description: Read-only dashboard aggregates under `/api/v1/analytics`. Each endpoint is guarded to exactly one role, so sign in as that role before running it. Decimal columns (`totalAmount`, `amount`) are aggregated to plain numbers in the response.

request.description: Requires `ADMIN`. Platform totals: technician and customer counts, service counts, booking counts by status, and revenue / refunds summed over PAID and REFUNDED payments.
Requires `CUSTOMER`. Booking totals for the caller, upcoming / completed / cancelled counts, and total spent and refunded.

Requires `TECHNICIAN`. Availability and slot counts, bookings by status, earnings and refunds, and the current rating and review count. Requires a technician profile to exist — run Create Technician Profile first.
